ai_pane_desc: Select text in your document, then click a button. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> in the editor to accept. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> undoes it.
ai_pane_placeholder: Your AI suggestion will appear here…
aitext_btn_title: Mark every AI-inserted passage directly in the document
backup_btn_title: Save a copy of all your work to your computer
backup_desc: Your documents, citations and projects live only in this browser. Clearing the browser data erases them. Download a backup file now and then, and keep it somewhere safe. It never contains your AI key or access code.
backup_done: Backup downloaded ✓ Keep the file somewhere safe.
backup_nudge_new: You have written {w} words and never made a backup. Clearing this browser would erase them.
backup_nudge_old: Your last backup is {n} days old. Save a fresh copy of your work?
bk_done_locked: Locked backup downloaded ✓ Keep the passphrase safe: it cannot be recovered.
bk_err_match: The two entries do not match.
bk_err_wrong: Wrong passphrase, or the file is damaged. Try again.
bk_h_create: Choose a passphrase for this backup
bk_last_verify: Last time you checked a backup file: {d}.
bk_lost_h: If you lose this phone or computer
bk_lost_p1: Your documents live only in this browser, on this device. No server holds a copy. If the device is lost, broken or reset, a backup file is the only way back. Keep the newest file in a second place: email it to yourself, put it in a cloud drive, or copy it to another device. A locked backup is safe to leave in email or a cloud drive, because only the passphrase opens it.
bk_lost_p2: To get your work back on a new device, open this site, go to Settings, press Restore from backup and choose the file. Check once, today, that your file opens: press Check a backup file.
bk_m_create: The file is locked on this device with your passphrase. The passphrase is never saved or sent anywhere, so if you forget it nobody can open the file, and that includes us. Write it down somewhere safe. Use at least 10 characters; a few unrelated words work well.
bk_m_open: Type the passphrase you chose when you made the file.
bk_never_verify: You have not checked a backup file yet. Checking one proves you can get your work back.
bk_nocrypto: This browser cannot lock files here. Open the app at its https address, or use the plain backup.
bk_verify_bad: That file cannot be read as an Appuscholar backup.
bk_verify_ok: This backup file can be read: {n} document(s), about {w} words, saved {d}. Nothing in the app was changed.
cap_desc: Adds "Figure 1" or "Table 1" with a title above the picture or table, in APA 7 style. Click a picture or a table, or put the cursor where the caption should go. Numbers update by themselves.
cc_desc: Compares the citations in your text with your reference list. It lists every source cited but missing from the list, and every list entry that is never cited. It runs on this computer and uses no AI.
cc_missing_h: Cited in the text but missing from the list
cc_near_name: The list has a similar name: {n} ({y}). Check the spelling.
cc_near_year: The list has {n} with a different year ({y}). Check the year.
cc_none_missing: None. Every citation has a list entry.
cc_none_unused: None. Every list entry is cited.
cc_note: Matching uses the first author's surname and the year. It reads APA-style citations such as (Smith, 2020), (Smith & Lee, 2020; Jones et al., 2019) and Smith (2020). A list entry is one paragraph, written like "Smith, J. (2020). Title."
cc_src_doc: Reference list used: the "{h}" section of this document ({n} entries).
cc_src_lib: This document has no References section yet, so your Citation Library ({n} sources) is used as the list.
cc_src_none: There is no reference list to compare with. Add a References section to the document, or add sources to your library.
cc_sum: {c} sources cited in the text. {m} not in the list. {u} list entries never cited.
cc_unread: List entries that could not be read: {n} (no surname before a comma, or no year in brackets). They are left out of the check.
cc_unused_h: In the list but never cited
chat_input_placeholder: Ask… e.g. Give me 3 title ideas
chat_panel_desc: Your purple study buddy — ask anything about your writing. Each reply has an "Insert into document" button.
cite_bib_fmt_num: Reference list inserted, numbered in library order ✓
cite_bookmarklet_desc: Like Zotero's browser button — drag this link to your bookmarks bar once. Then, on any journal article, PubMed or arXiv page, click it to send that page's citation straight into your library here.
cite_bookmarklet_note: Drag — don't click — the button above onto your bookmarks bar. It only reads standard citation tags already on the page (the same ones Zotero and Mendeley use); it can't read pages that don't publish them, like most news sites.
cite_lookup_btn: 🔎 Fill from DOI, link, PubMed ID or title
cite_lookup_empty: Paste a DOI, a link, a PubMed ID or a title first
cite_lookup_fail: Could not reach Crossref. Please fill it in by hand.
cite_lookup_nf: Not found on Crossref. Please fill it in by hand.
cite_lookup_nopmid: Could not find a DOI for that PubMed ID. Paste the DOI or the title instead.
cite_lookup_ok: Found ✓ The DOI and every other box below are now filled. Check them, then press + Library
cite_not_used: Not cited in any of your documents yet
cite_note_check: Formats follow the published manuals as best I know them. Check one entry per style against the manual or your journal's rules.
cite_note_numbered: Numbered style: the number is the source's place in your library. Vancouver, IEEE and AMA number by first appearance in the text, so check the order before you submit.
cite_num_unsaved: This source is not in your library yet, so its number is a guess. Add it to the library to fix the number.
cite_panel_desc: Add a source, then insert citations as you write.
cite_quote_desc: A Hindi source is quoted as written. An English source is translated automatically when your content language is set to Hindi, and marked (अनुवादित) with the original kept on hover.
cite_quote_placeholder: Paste the exact quoted text here…
cite_sharing_note: 🤝 Class sharing: export your library and share the file with classmates — import theirs to build one shared collection. Your documents and writing style stay on your own device.
cite_url_label: Link, DOI or full reference: paste it here and the form fills itself
cite_usage_summary_fmt: {c} of {n} sources are cited in your documents. {u} not cited yet.
continue_btn_title: AI writes the next ~120 words for you
design_panel_desc: Plan your method, pick the right regulatory path, and prepare consent, ethics committee and registration paperwork before data collection starts. Everything below is a starting checklist, not a legal ruling — confirm the final requirement with your own institution's Ethics Committee.
devil_btn_title: Argues against your passage the way a critical reviewer would. Nothing in the reply is meant to be pasted in.
devil_label: A critical reviewer might say this. Answer each point in your own words. Nothing here is meant to be pasted in.
devil_need: Select or write a passage of at least a few sentences first.
devil_ready: Challenges ready in the AI pane
df_btn_title: Write first. The AI then asks questions about your writing instead of writing for you.
df_label: Feedback on your draft. Nothing here is meant to be pasted in, so the writing stays yours.
df_need_sel: Select the passage you want feedback on first.
df_need_text: Write at least a few sentences first. Then ask for feedback.
df_on: Draft first is ON. The AI will ask questions about your writing and will not write for you.
df_ready: Questions ready in the AI pane
doc_import_title: Import a .docx, .pdf, .txt or .html file as a new document — or just drag one onto the editor
editor_placeholder: Start writing here… Select text and press Improve, or just write and let AI continue.
erase_fail: Could not delete your account. Check your connection and try again.
erase_intro: Everything under your account is deleted: projects, documents and their versions, keys and the AI-use log. This cannot be undone. Export first if you want a copy.
export_fail: Could not make the export. Check your connection and try again.
extend_btn_title: Select some text first, then click to extend it
faq_a_broken: Try a hard refresh — Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac — or open it in Chrome or Edge if you're on something else. Both render this app best.
faq_a_code: Paste the whole code, including the dot in the middle, with no extra spaces or line breaks — copying from some apps adds a stray character at the start or end. Codes also expire; if the date has passed, you'll need a fresh one from whoever gave you Appuscholar.
faq_a_hindi: A few things stay in English on purpose — statistical test names, citation style names (APA, MLA), and the external AI-provider sign-up pages — since those are the exact terms you'll meet everywhere else too. Anything other than that is a genuine bug worth reporting below.
faq_a_key: Your AI key is kept in this browser, or locked with your passphrase under your account. If the app says there is no key, open ⚙ AI Provider / Key and paste it again.
faq_a_lost: Your documents are saved under your account with every version, so clearing a browser does not lose them. Sign in on any device to find them. If a document is missing, check the Doc list and Research Projects, then write to us.
faq_q_broken: 🖥 The page looks broken, or won't load properly
faq_q_hindi: हि Something stayed in English after switching to Hindi
faq_q_key: 🔌 My AI key stopped working, or I lost it
faq_q_lost: 💾 My work disappeared after closing the tab or clearing my browser
help_contact_intro: Still stuck? Tell us what happened and we'll help directly.
help_contact_unset: A direct contact option isn't set up yet — for now, reach whoever gave you Appuscholar.
help_intro: Most problems have a quick fix below. Check here first — it's faster than waiting on an email.
idea_constraints_placeholder: Budget, known ethics concerns, requirements your supervisor or department has set…
idea_panel_desc: Before you commit to a topic, talk it through here. Describe what you want to study and what you actually have available — the advisor below judges whether it's realistic, not just whether it's interesting.
idea_panel_note: This gives an honest outside read on your idea, not approval — the AI can be wrong, and a real supervisor's judgment still matters most. Once the plan feels solid, head to the Research tab next to find a research gap and ground it in real literature.
idea_resources_label: What you actually have access to
idea_resources_placeholder: Participants you can realistically recruit, facilities, equipment, software, a supervisor's lab…
idea_saveproject_btn: 💾 Save this idea as a project
idea_timeframe_placeholder: e.g. one semester, 3 months, by April
idea_topic_label: Your working idea or research question
idea_topic_placeholder: e.g. Does sleep quality predict exam performance in college students?
ie_cap_exists: This picture already has a caption.
ie_desc: Turn, crop, lighten or darken, and hide a participant's identity. Everything happens on this device.
ie_fail: Could not edit this picture. Try inserting it again from a file.
ie_h_bar: Drag a box over the eyes, or over the whole face. It is filled black. A black bar hides identity far more safely than pixels.
ie_h_bg: Drag a box around the person. Everything outside an oval inside that box turns into the plain colour. This is a manual outline, not an automatic cut-out.
ie_h_crop: Drag a box around the part to keep.
ie_h_none: Pick a tool above, then drag on the picture.
ie_h_pix: Drag a box over the area to pixelate. Pixelation can sometimes be partly undone, so for faces a black bar is safer.
ie_note_bar: Eyes or face were covered with a black bar to protect the participant's identity.
ie_note_bg: The background was replaced with a plain colour.
ie_note_pix: Part of the face was pixelated to protect the participant's identity.
img_missing: {n} picture(s) in this document could not be found in this browser. Restore from a backup to bring them back.
imp_note: A paper by someone else is kept as a source. It is not counted as your writing, not used to learn your style and not shown in "% yours". You can change this later with the 📄 button.
imp_pdf_toast: PDF imported as a source paper, not counted as your writing. Change it with the 📄 button.
import_v1_vault: Your backup is read on this computer and saved locked in your vault.
improve_btn_title: Select some text first, then click to polish its grammar
latex_btn_title: Download as a LaTeX file (.tex), the format some universities and journals ask for. It opens in Overleaf. Skip this unless you have been told you need it.
login_intro: This copy needs an access code. Paste the code you were given below — it's checked on this computer, nothing is uploaded.
login_note: Don't have a code, or has yours expired? Ask whoever gave you Appuscholar for a new one.
nc_btn: 🔢 Check the numbers in my document
nc_c_df: The degrees of freedom must be positive.
nc_c_form: A p-value must lie between 0 and 1.
nc_c_onetail: The reported p is about half of the recomputed one. Was a one-tailed test used? If so, say so in the text.
nc_c_round: The gap is small. A rounding slip or a rounded statistic can cause it. Check your output.
nc_c_typo: A typo in the statistic, the df or the p-value is the most common cause. Check them against your output.
nc_c_zero: p can never be exactly zero. Write p < .001.
nc_desc: Finds the statistics written in your document (t, F, χ², r, z and H, with their df and p), works out the p-value again from the test statistic and df, and flags any that do not match. It runs on this computer and uses no AI.
nc_none: No statistics found. This check reads the APA pattern, for example "t(21) = 2.15, p = .043".
nc_note: The check allows for rounding of the statistic. It reads only statistics written in the usual APA order, with p straight after the statistic. A consistent result does not show that the right test was used.
nc_sum: Found {n}: {ok} consistent, {w} not consistent ({e} change the conclusion).
num_missing_fmt: Numbers cited in this document with no source in your library: {n}.
oa_tip_bronze: Bronze: free on the publisher's site right now, but with no open licence, so the publisher could remove it.
oa_tip_gold: Gold: the whole journal is free to read, so this paper is free on the publisher's own site.
oa_tip_green: Green: a free copy of the author's own version sits in an online repository.
oa_tip_hybrid: Hybrid: this paper is free to read in a journal that otherwise charges for access.
org_badge_title: Marked as someone else's paper. Not counted in your % yours, My writing or writing samples.
org_btn_title_own: Tell the app this document is someone else's paper, so it is not counted as your writing.
org_btn_title_src: This document is marked as someone else's paper. Click to mark it as your own writing.
org_toast_src: Marked as a source paper. It no longer counts as your writing.
pop_blocked: Your browser blocked the new window. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.
pop_btn_title: Open this tool in its own window, for a second screen
pop_nowin: The writing window is not open.
pop_unsupported: Only Citations and Research can open in their own window.
project_bar_empty: No research project yet — working in scratch space
projects_empty: No research projects saved yet. Work normally, then use "Save as research project" whenever you want to track a stage and come back to it later.
prov_desc: Where the words in your documents came from. It counts text typed in this editor against text inserted from an AI suggestion or the chat. It cannot see your thinking, and text you retype from an AI answer counts as yours. No targets, no score. It is just a mirror.
prov_doc_fmt: {n} words, typed here {t}%. AI passages: {p} ({k} left as inserted, {e} edited{u}).
prov_src_line: {w} words in {n} source paper(s) are left out of these counts.
prov_total: All documents: {w} words. Typed here {t}%, inserted from AI {a}%.
prov_trend: Share typed here, at the end of each week
prov_trend_none: The weekly picture builds up as you keep writing.
ps_done: Done: put it in my document
ps_h_arrow: Drag from the tail to the point of the arrow.
ps_h_blur: Drag a box over the area to blur. A black bar hides identity far more safely than a blur.
ps_h_rect: Drag a box to outline something. Colour and size are at the right of this bar.
ps_h_text: Type the text above, then click where it should go.
ps_nochan: This browser cannot open the photo studio. Using the small editor instead.
ps_noparent: The document window is not listening. Keep the Appuscholar tab open, or use Save a copy.
ps_note_blur: Part of the face was blurred to protect the participant's identity.
ps_openhint: Press Open a picture to start.
ps_text_ph: Text to place, then click the picture
psych_panel_desc: Select the text you want analyzed (or leave nothing selected to use the whole document).
psych_panel_note: Paste raw SPSS / JASP / R output and use Format results in APA to get correct APA 7th reporting.
qual_empty_note: No codes yet — add one above, then select text in your document and tap it to tag that passage.
qual_panel_desc: Select a passage in your document, then tap a code below to tag it. Build codes under other codes to group related ideas. Works across every document you have, not just the one that's open.
qual_passages_desc: Every passage tagged with this code, across all your documents.
qual_show_colors_label: Show code colors in the document
rc_doi_missing: No DOI saved. The match below came from a title search:
rc_empty: Add a source to your library first.
rc_fail: Could not reach Crossref right now. Try again in a moment.
rc_nf: Not found in Crossref. Check the DOI, title and author, or the source may simply not be indexed there.
rc_ok: Found in Crossref and the details match.
rc_summary_fmt: Checked {n} sources against Crossref: {o} match, {d} differ, {f} not found. Books, reports, theses and Hindi sources are often not in Crossref, so "not found" is a prompt to look again, not proof the source is wrong.
recap_toggle: Show a recap and three questions when I return after five days or more
research_connected_desc: Pick one OpenAlex paper above and see what it cites and what has cited it — a quick way to trace a research thread.
research_external_desc: Google Scholar, JSTOR and most publisher sites don't allow apps like this one to fetch results automatically — they have to be searched in your browser. These open a new tab with your topic already typed in.
research_external_summary: 🌐 Not finding it? Search Google Scholar and others directly
research_grounded_note: Drafted strictly from the papers you checked above — always verify the actual sources before citing them.
research_manual_desc: Found something on Google Scholar or a journal site? Enter its details here to drop it straight into your Citation Manager library.
research_manual_summary: ➕ Add a paper you found elsewhere
research_panel_desc: Search OpenAlex and PubMed live, free, no install — pick what's relevant, then draft a literature review or find a research gap, grounded only in the abstracts you found.
restore_bad: That file is not an Appuscholar backup.
restore_confirm:

ret_did: Before you left you had recorded:
ret_nolog: No activity was recorded since your last visit.
ret_q1: In your own words, what is the main question your study is answering right now?
ret_q2: What is the next concrete thing you will do on this project?
ret_q3: What is the weakest part of your work right now, and why?
ret_q_intro: Answer in your own words. Nobody grades these, and the app does not read them. They are saved on this computer so you can see how your thinking moved.
retr_added_warn: Added, but this paper is marked as retracted. Check before citing it.
retr_failed: Could not run the retraction check right now. Try again in a moment.
retr_lib_warn: OpenAlex marks this source as retracted. Check the publisher's notice before you cite it.
retr_nodoi: None of your sources has a DOI, so there is nothing to check.
retr_summary_fmt: Checked {c} sources with a DOI for retractions: {r} flagged. {n} without a DOI could not be checked. No flag does not prove a paper is sound.
retr_tip: OpenAlex marks this paper as retracted. Check the publisher's notice before you cite it.
rs_inserted: Citation inserted and saved to your library ✓
rt_col_gone: The column “{c}” is not in the loaded data any more, so this test cannot be repeated.
rt_desc: Every result inserted from the Statistics Lab carries a hidden tag that remembers which test it came from and which data it was run on. This list compares each tagged result with the latest data loaded under the same dataset name. A result marked out of date was run on data that has since changed.
rt_ds_help: Results you insert are tagged with this name. If you later load changed data under the same name, the tagged results in your document are flagged as out of date.
rt_edit_warn: Re-running replaces your edited text with the new sentence. Continue?
rt_edited: You edited this sentence after inserting it.
rt_failed: The test could not be run on the current data.
rt_load_first: Load the changed data first: paste it in the Statistics Lab, name it “{n}” and press Parse data.
rt_none: No tagged results in the open document. Results inserted from the Statistics Lab from now on are tagged.
rt_note: The app cannot tell which words in your paragraph depended on a number. After a re-run, reread the text around it. Tables, charts and figures made earlier are not tagged and are not checked.
rt_sig_flip: The conclusion at .05 has changed. Read the paragraph around this sentence again.
rt_sum: {n} tagged results: {c} current, {s} out of date, {u} not checkable.
rt_why_norec: This tag has no record in this browser (the document came from another browser, or saved records were cleared).
rt_why_noset: The dataset “{n}” has not been loaded in this browser, so there is nothing to compare with. Load it in the Statistics Lab under the same name.
rt_why_stale: The data under this name changed on {d}. The number in the text was calculated before that.

sap_mode_existing: Add to an existing research project
sap_stage_desc: Guessed from the tool you had open — change it if that's wrong.

settings_intro: Pick one. Your key is saved in this browser and sent only to the provider you choose.
settings_keymode_label: How should this key be stored?
settings_keymode_pass: 🔒 Protect with a passphrase — safest (type it once per session)
settings_keymode_plain: Remember on this computer — easiest, no passphrase
settings_keymode_session: This tab only — forget when I close it (college computer)
settings_orcid_label: Your researcher ID number — ORCID iD (optional, printed on exports and templates)
settings_orcid_link: Don't have one? Get a free ORCID iD →

settings_pack_psychology: Psychology — adds the Research helpers tab
settings_warn: ⚠ Because this app runs as a local file, every HTML file on your computer shares one storage area. A key saved with Remember on this computer can be read by any other HTML file you open. The passphrase option encrypts it so those files see only scrambled text.

slides_panel_h3: 🖥 Make a PPT from this document

terms_age: I am 18 years old or older. Appuscholar is not for anyone younger.
terms_agree: I have read this and I agree.
terms_d1: Your documents, sources and projects are saved on Appuscholar's server under your account, with every version kept, so you can open them from any device. The people who run Appuscholar can see them only to keep the service running and will not read them for any other purpose. Statistics data is encrypted with a passphrase only you know before it leaves your browser.
terms_d2: Your AI key stays in this browser, or on the server locked with a passphrase only you know. When you press an AI button, the key travels with that one request to the provider you chose, is used once, and is not kept.
terms_d3: When you press an AI button, the text you selected travels through Appuscholar's server straight to that provider (Google, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, OpenAI or Anthropic). Appuscholar does not keep it. The provider's own terms apply, and on a free key a provider may read or reuse what it receives. Never send names, phone numbers, roll numbers or other details that identify a participant.
terms_d4: Paper search sends your search words, DOI or ORCID iD to OpenAlex, Crossref, PubMed and ORCID. The fonts and the Word and PDF tools load with the app from Appuscholar's own address, which can see your IP address, as any website can.
terms_leave: You cannot use Appuscholar without accepting. To leave, close this browser tab.
terms_reopen_btn: Terms and where your data goes
terms_u1: It is a writing and research helper. It is not medical, psychological or legal advice. A score on a screening scale is not a diagnosis.
terms_u2: AI suggestions, plagiarism checks and AI detectors are only indicators, and they can be wrong. Check every citation and every number yourself.
terms_u3: You are responsible for your ethics approval, your participants' consent, your institution's rules on AI help, and for saying where AI helped.
terms_u4: Appuscholar is free and comes as it is, with no promise that it is correct or always available.
terms_under_msg: Appuscholar is for people aged 18 and over. Please close this page. If you are studying, ask your teacher or your institution which tools they allow.
terms_use_h: What Appuscholar is, and is not

vault_recovered: Vault recovered ✓ — a new recovery sheet is ready

vault_setup_h2: Protect your work with a passphrase
vault_setup_intro: Your documents are saved under your account, locked so that only this passphrase opens them. Nobody at Appuscholar can read them. Titles and project names stay readable so your lists work. If you lose the passphrase and the recovery sheet, the documents cannot be recovered.
vault_sheet_intro: If you forget the passphrase, this code is the only way back in. Save the file somewhere safe. Appuscholar does not keep a copy.
vault_unlock_hint: Type the passphrase that protects your documents.
vault_wrong: Wrong passphrase — nothing was unlocked. Try again.
viva_aud_conf: A panel or audience at a conference
viva_aud_viva: An examiner at my viva or defence
viva_btn_title: Practise answering an examiner's question about your writing, with no AI help in the answer box
viva_desc: The AI asks one question an examiner might ask about the passage you selected (or the end of your document). Answer from your own head. There is no AI help in the answer box, because the point is to rehearse the real moment.
viva_need: Select or write a passage of at least a few sentences first.
viva_ph: Type your answer, as if you were speaking.
vz_bar_key_ci: Bars = group means. Error bars = 95% confidence interval. Dots = each participant.
vz_bar_key_none: Bars = group means. Dots = each participant.
vz_bar_key_sd: Bars = group means. Error bars = one standard deviation. Dots = each participant.
vz_bar_key_se: Bars = group means. Error bars = one standard error. Dots = each participant.
vz_bar_zero: Bars show size by their length, so a bar axis should start at zero. Starting higher makes small differences look large.
vz_box_key: Box = middle half of scores. Thick line = median. Diamond = mean. Whiskers reach the furthest score within 1.5 box-lengths. Open circles = unusual scores beyond that. Dots = each participant.
vz_desc: Paste your data (first row = column names) or use the data from the Statistics Lab. Pick a chart. Every chart is drawn on this computer and can be saved for your paper.
vz_hist_key: Bars count scores in each range. Dashed curve = the normal curve with the same mean and spread. Skewness = {s} (0 is symmetric; beyond about 1 or below -1 is clearly lopsided).
vz_img_fail: Could not make the picture. Try the SVG download.
vz_no_lab: Parse some data in the Statistics Lab first, or paste it here.
vz_nodata: No numbers to draw yet. Check that you picked a score column with numbers.
vz_open_btn: 📈 Research figures (box plot, error bars, histogram, Q-Q)
vz_qq_key: Dots close to the dashed line mean the scores are close to a normal distribution. Bends at the ends suggest skew or outliers. With very few scores, expect wobble.
vz_t_bar: Bar of means with error bars
vz_title_in: Draw the title inside the picture
welcome_intro: A writing and research assistant, with psychology research support built in. Everything you write is saved under your account.
welcome_step1: Click ⚙ AI Provider / Key at the top right.
welcome_step2: Pick Google Gemini or Groq — both have a free tier.
welcome_step3: Follow the link, create a key, paste it in, press Save Key.
welcome_step4: Start writing. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to accept a suggestion.
welcome_warn: Appuscholar drafts and checks — it does not do your thinking. Verify every citation, and check your institution's policy on AI assistance before you submit.
writingsample_clear_confirm: Delete the writing samples saved so far? This only clears the private copy used for the future style trainer — your actual documents are untouched.
writingsample_desc: Appuscholar privately saves a copy of your own writing from each document on this computer — whatever you typed yourself, skipping anything an AI suggestion inserted. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. The idea is a future tool that learns to write in your own voice from this. Turn off any time; your documents themselves are never affected either way.
writingsample_label: Help build my writing-style trainer (coming later)
writingsample_status_fmt: {n} document(s) saved so far, {w} words of your own writing captured.
writingsample_status_off: Off — nothing is being saved for this right now.
